task: Core #1186 F6-U03p: genuine PG17 nonparticipant, leave and entitlement-revocation Office RLS regression

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Bounded PG17 local RLS regression over immutable original 78 SQL sources; no hosted provider Auth proof or migration/SQL DDL changes; positive/negative thread-message-task cases and rollback per test transaction.

acceptanceCriteria: Immutable F6-U03k 78 original Git SQL replay and F6-U03n role/two-tenant positive fixture pass before the new unit.
Same-store support member not participating in private Pro thread can read customer thread, message and task, but not private thread, message or task; B owner can read both.
Same-store viewer cannot read either Office thread type while B owner is a positive control.
After private participant leaves, current B owner retains B customer communication but immediately loses B private thread, message and task until rollback.
After role revoked or expired, authenticated browser gets zero B Office threads/messages/tasks, with authorized A owner rows visible in a separate control transaction.
Expired Alap officeCommunication feature denies A customer Office rows, without hiding B Pro control rows.
Pro-to-Alap downgrade retains B customer Office and denies internal chat, even with manual override, with A Alap support positive preserved.

All browser reads use actual non-BYPASSRLS SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated with synthetic transaction-local claim, unfiltered selects of threads, messages, tasks, and explicit positive and negative identifiers.
Fail closed on empty positive fixtures, unexpected rows, malformed/missing cases or psql errors; no hosted changes, not signed Supabase JWT, no provider release claim.
invariants: Only additive scripts, Vitest, workflow and documentation; original SQL source, JWT shim, migrations, RLS policies and grants untouched.
No service_role/postgres browser-query evidence, no role bypass and no synthetic JWT claim represented as provider-issued.
Every regression case has a real positive data control and at least one negative row outcome.
Temporary role/entitlement/member changes are confined to ROLLBACK transactions in disposable local PG17.
Alap customer communication preserved outside specific, intentionally expired entitlement case.
forbiddenStates: Entire Office reads return no rows but validator marks successful positive cases.
Nonparticipant, viewer or deauthorized user sees seeded private/customer Office rows while case passes.
Participant exit, revoked or expired role, entitlement expiry, or downgrade leaves a prohibited thread/message/task accessible.
A test changes one of 78 SQL source migrations, enables staging or writes hosted database data.
An implementation says signed Supabase JWT or managed Data API/Storage are proven by local claim GUC.

failureModes: SQL trigger side effect unexpectedly replaces fixture roles or entitlements during downgrade.
A support member is wrongly granted private access by support role, bypassing participant membership.
Revoked or expired role is accepted by cache, token or helper despite RLS session re-evaluation.
Messages or tasks have weaker rules than threads, leaking private content after thread hidden.
Transient mutation does not roll back, contaminating subsequent cases.
Role probe accidentally runs as postgres or role not recorded, creating a false positive.
All reads return zero and the harness incorrectly reports security PASS.
edgeCases: Viewer must be a valid same-store viewer, distinct from unbound stranger.
Different permission models for customer and private internal threads; participant exit must not block customer support.
Manual Alap teamChat entitlement remains seeded and must not override actual plan.
Revoked_at and valid_until are separately checked, not conflated.
Pro-to-Alap downgrade may trigger entitlement sync; actual observable customer support must remain.
Each row probe has unfiltered per-table thread-ID evidence, not count-only.
Authenticated role must be non-BYPASSRLS, uid must match transaction-local synthetic claim.

specialistReviews.finding: Postgres fixture mutations can be mistaken for browser permissions, while data with zero-row fixtures appears secure.
specialistReviews.resolution: Mutations only under superuser on disposable fixture; actual SELECT under authenticated non-BYPASSRLS and positive existing identifiers in every case.

specialistReviews.finding: Lifecycle testing can permanently change fixture or trigger sensitive side-effects.
specialistReviews.resolution: Transaction-local fixture mutations roll back; prior source-proven two-tenant row evidence is required before each post-transition suite.

specialistReviews.finding: Local simulation is not Auth JWT revocation or provider PostgREST proof.
specialistReviews.resolution: Machine verdict and docs mark provider-issued JWT, Data API, Storage, hosted release strictly unproven.

specialistReviews.finding: A target unit could silently shadow original source bootstrap or suppress browser SELECT failures.
specialistReviews.resolution: Preserve same 78 checked Git blobs, run original F6-U03n/F6-U03o positive and negative proof and ON_ERROR_STOP on all PostgreSQL calls before new staged checks.

challenge.scenario: A same-store member without private-thread participant is incorrectly allowed via tenant owner/support status.
challenge.finding: Tenant membership must not replace private participation.
challenge.resolution: Require support user's B customer row positive and B private negative for all Office tables; B participant owner positive.

challenge.scenario: Role/entitlement expiry suppresses all Office data and validator reports PASS.
challenge.resolution: Assert baseline and side-by-side authorized tenant row positive evidence and exact expected per-table IDs in all cases.

challenge.scenario: One of three Office relations leaks data after membership leaves.
challenge.resolution: Independent unfiltered identifiers from threads, messages and tasks compared to exact expected IDs.

challenge.scenario: A native SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated with synthetic GUC is reported as provider-issued Supabase JWT proof.
challenge.finding: Signed-JWT provenance would be falsely elevated to release authority.
challenge.resolution: Report providerSignedJWT=false and hostedTouched=false, and maintain separate provider acceptance.

challenge.scenario: Role revocation causes B owner zero rows, and no valid actor's positive read is captured.
challenge.finding: An all-deny failure is indistinguishable from correct RLS.
challenge.resolution: Bind A owner real customer row positive within each deny-only scenario and reject any missing control.

challenge.scenario: Only office_threads denies a private row while office_messages/tasks continue leaking content.
challenge.resolution: Capture unfiltered thread ID lists independently from all three source tables and compare exact expected identities.

challenge.scenario: SQL lifecycle update persists and changes subsequent evidence.
challenge.finding: Fixture tests are not independent and alter baseline.
challenge.resolution: Run each reversible update in its own BEGIN/ROLLBACK, recheck clean positive source baseline and local identity guard, never COMMIT role transition.

challenge.scenario: A role viewer is confused with unrelated user, or support is granted private access because organization role has broad permissions.
challenge.resolution: Insert two distinct same-store active role bindings, require viewer zero and support customer positive with private negative and B owner full positive.

proofPlan: Read original canonical guard/known failures and pass exact task Plan Before Code before first implementation edit.
Re-run 78 untouched original SQL Git sources under identity-verified disposable PG17, validate F6-U03n schema/role/tenant positives.
Add only transaction-local lifecycle probes and exact negative/positive row IDs for Office threads/messages/tasks.
Run adversarial unit validators, role and expired entitlement negative tests and real Docker17 SQL using psql ON_ERROR_STOP.
After edit-time/preflight/replay and full Quality/TypeScript/Build/Security, require exact-head Truth/Lifecycle and CI-emitted closed-plan identity; no automatic merge.
operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Verified F6-U03o real PG17 source-authentic tenant and anonymous/helper tests do not prove post-revocation or same-tenant nonparticipant access to threads, independent messages and tasks. Stale role, expired entitlement, private participant leave or Pro-to-Alap change might leave unauthorized rows visible despite static predicates. Extend the bounded local authenticated native-role tests with positive/negative controls and reversible fixture transitions. No hosted JWT or DB write authority.
observableOutcomes: Original immutable 78 Git migration sources, PG17 peer identity, canonical F6-U03n two-tenant and F6-U03o anonymous/helper proofs remain green before new tests.

Seed actual B-support and B-viewer authenticated users with valid B role bindings but no B private participant link; support reads real B customer threads/messages/tasks only, viewer sees none; B owner remains positive.

In reversible transactions test B participant leaving, B role revoked, B role expired, A customer entitlement expired and B Pro-to-Alap downgrade, checking exact Office thread/message/task IDs and same-session or same-fixture positive authorized tenant controls.
Record current_user authenticated, rolbypassrls=false and auth.uid equal to synthetic GUC for every query; fail if role missing, positive data absent or foreign/private row visible.
Adversarial unit checks reject any leak on one Office relation independently, denial-only no-data or forged role evidence.
Return local synthetic only with realSignedSupabaseJwtProven=false, managedDataApiProven=false, hostedTouched=false, releaseAuthorized=false.
Run independent Docker PG17 and full Quality/TypeScript/Build/Security, Completion Truth/Lifecycle exact-head before scoped closure.
unresolvedRisks: Synthetic transaction-local auth.uid lacks cryptographic Supabase Auth signature, JWT revocation, refresh and provider transport semantics.
Only selected B support/viewer, role expiration, participant leave and A/B plan scenarios are included; other permissions/ownership and business workflows remain separate.
Supabase hosted exposed-schema Data API, Storage, provider-specific service_role/RPC and TLS migration provisioning not exercised.
Any discovered source security leak requires separate reviewed forward-only migration and PO release gate, not alteration of test expectations.
